name: illustrations

version.prompts: P1 2026-11-08 PT (the seven Codex illustration reference prompts)
version.labels: L1 2026-11-08 PT (expected kind per reference; acceptable kinds are the older kinds that can carry the same idea)

measures: The Codex illustration primitives: right kind (tensor items in a transformation, token-links, block-stack, comparison of block stacks, flow with parallel paths), faithfulness to the sketch, render width (intrinsic width per diagram), the 320 px callout fallback on the tile.
written: 2026-11-08 PT, from the Codex handoff (illustration-primitives.md table of reference cards); not seen by any card
notation: As correct-svg: per-depth kinds / acceptableKinds / sketch; depth names on this tree are overview / standard / deep.

prompts.prompt: How does a transformer get query, key and value vectors from one token?

sketch: Core: One input vector strip feeds three separate learned projections into a query, a key and a value strip; each strip shows its dimension.
Optional: Cells showing excerpts of the vector values.

prompts.prompt: When the word sat attends to the sentence the cat sat on the mat, which words matter most?

sketch: Core: Two token rows with weighted arrows from sat to each word; the six weights sum to 1 and the strongest arrow (to cat) carries the visible maximum.
Optional: The repeated words kept as separate positions.

prompts.prompt: What is inside one transformer encoder layer and why is it repeated?

sketch: Core: One encoder layer opened up as self-attention, add and norm, feed-forward, add and norm, with a repeat count of six.
Optional: Token embeddings entering the stack.

prompts.prompt: What happens inside one Llama-style decoder block?

sketch: Core: Pre-normalization, grouped-query attention and a SwiGLU feed-forward with two residual adds and a repeat bracket.
Optional: The dimension note at Detailed.

prompts.prompt: How does a mixture-of-experts router choose the top two experts for one token?

sketch: Core: A router ranks the experts, two are run in parallel and the others skipped, and their outputs are blended with the shared expert.
Optional: Eight routed experts and one shared expert shown once each.
Core: One plot on shared axes: the observed points drawn once as scatter, a simple-fit line and an overfit line, and one labelled held-out point the overfit line misses.
Optional: Axis labels naming the input and the target; a caption saying what to notice.

prompts.want: multi-series coordinate-plot: observed scatter + simple-fit line + overfit line + one annotated held-out point; the sentence before the plot points at it

paraphrases: How does cross-validation tell me a model is overfitting?
Why compare training and validation error across k folds?
Can k-fold cross-validation show that my model memorizes the data?
What does a gap between training error and validation error per fold mean?
Explain cross-validation and how it exposes overfitting.

sketch: Core: One grouped bar-chart: for each fold (categories 1 to 5) a training-error bar and a validation-error bar, with a steady gap between them (validation above training in every fold).
Optional: A unit on the value axis; a caption saying the size of the gap is the signal. Never a line chart across folds: the folds are categories, not a quantity that varies.

prompts.want: grouped bar-chart (variant grouped, categories = folds, two series: training error and validation error) with a steady gap; the sentence before the chart points at the gap; never a coordinate-plot line across folds
